one_liner: Own-IDL C++/Java/Python serialization framework; bit-packed decode 1.2x-2.6x faster than protoc.
what_it_does: Zserio is a schema-driven serialization framework with its own IDL (.zs files, not .proto), compiled by a Java-based compiler into C++, Java, or Python code that links against a matching Zserio runtime library. Generated types expose read/write against a bit-level stream, plus optional JSON import/export, SQLite table mapping, reflection, and gRPC/MQTT service and pub-sub stubs. It is not a protobuf drop-in: schema language, generated API shape, and wire format all differ from protoc's.
how_it_is_fast: Zserio packs fields at the bit level rather than byte level, and its default schemas carry no per-field tag IDs or explicit length prefixes the way protobuf's wire format does, so there is less to scan per field during decode. Byte-aligning fields (the '_align' schema variants) trades blob size for speed by removing bit-shift work, cutting decode time roughly another 40-45% versus the default schema on addressbook and carsales in this benchmark. No SIMD or algorithmic trick is documented; the win is wire-format layout, not a decode algorithm.
when_to_use: Designing a new wire format from scratch where blob size matters as much as decode speed
Multi-language C++/Java/Python project willing to author .zs schemas instead of .proto
Need built-in SQLite table serialization, JSON debug export, or generic reflection/services without hand-rolling them
Functional-safety-conscious C++ codebase: C++11 runtime, >600 unit tests, ASan/UBSan clean, 99% line coverage
Deserialize-heavy workloads (parse once, read many) where a 1.2x-2.6x per-decode win compounds
when_not_to_use: Already invested in protobuf schemas, tooling, or cross-org interop; migration cost likely exceeds the modest measured speedup
Need protobuf-style forward/backward field compatibility; Zserio's compactness comes partly from dropping field IDs and lengths
Team can't add a Java-based external compiler step (zserio.jar) to the build
Need platforms beyond 64/32-bit Linux and 64-bit Windows; macOS/ARM are not in the stated Supported Platforms list
Want a larger, independently verified speedup: siblings RapidProto (~7x) and vtprotobuf (~1.7x) show bigger measured wins over protoc

integration.dependencies: none for the C++ runtime itself; bundled SQLite3 only if using the SQL-database extension; Java (JRE) needed at build time to run the zserio.jar code generator, not at runtime
integration.min_toolchain: C++11; gcc 7.5.0+ (11.4.0/7.5.0 tested), clang 11.0.0+ (14.0.6/21.1.8 tested), MinGW 7.5.0+, MSVC 2017+; CMake 3.15+ if using the bundled CMake helper
integration.platforms: 64-bit Linux, 32-bit Linux, 64-bit Windows per README's Supported Platforms list; macOS/ARM not stated
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false — different IDL (.zs vs .proto), different generated API, different wire format

gotchas: Byte-aligned (_align) and delta-packed (_packed) schema variants trade blob size against decode speed in opposite directions; pick per workload
Compact wire format omits field tags/lengths, so schema-evolution/compatibility rules differ sharply from protobuf's
Code generated by the zserio compiler inherits the license of the input .zs schema, separate from the BSD-3-Clause runtime license
Open issue #577 'Consider to optimize C++ serialization performance' (still open) indicates maintainers see further headroom
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Zserio when you want a full schema framework (SQLite mapping, JSON debug strings, services/pub-sub, one schema for C++/Java/Python) and can move off .proto. Pick RapidProto or vtprotobuf instead if you must keep .proto files and want a bigger measured decode speedup with less schema-language lock-in.
verified_claims_summary: Per-decode time (protobuf ParseFromString vs zserio read, pre-serialized blob, JSON load/serialize untimed) on 4 schemas, gcc 11.3.0 CMake-Release build, Intel i7-9850H/Linux Mint 21.1: Zserio beat protoc-generated C++ by 1.17x-2.63x (addressbook 1.478 vs 1.731ms, apollo 0.244 vs 0.641ms, carsales 1.374 vs 2.053ms, simpletrace 0.221 vs 0.386ms); byte-aligned variants reached 2.05x and 2.22x. Benchmark is first-party (same org as Zserio, 6-star companion repo), evidence tier C.
status_note: Active (last commit 2026-09-17, frequent releases); BSD-3-Clause runtime, with generated code separately licensed under the input schema's license.
